summary: Umatilla NF crow's-nest tree lookout of the 1930s, dismantled in 1949 per one account; the Forest Service guard station here is now a rental cabin.

facts.design: Crow's nest tree platform; one account describes a small platform up a rickety ladder in an old white fir about 300 feet from the house
facts.status_note: The lookout tree is gone; the Forest Service guard station cabin still stands and is rented, but no source says whether it sits on the lookout spot

access.note: The Forest Service rents the Summit Guard Station bunkhouse to anyone who books; no source describes public access to the lookout site itself

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umatilla National Forest

events.note: Fireman-lookout Bill Monroe on duty, per a September 1931 account quoted on the Forest Lookouts page
Civilian Conservation Corps built a two-story residence, garage, gas house and barn at the Forest Service station (not the lookout tree)
Summit Cabin built as a guard station; this is the rental cabin, not the lookout tree
Old Summit Tree Tower dismantled for safety reasons (Pendleton Ranger District annual report, entry dated March 17, 1949, as quoted)
Registered August 21, 2011 as US 1137, OR 492; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com describe a 1930s crow's nest tree platform; the Forest Lookouts page quotes a 1939 memoir about a platform in an old white fir and a 1949 'Summit Tree Tower'; the Forest Service page covers only the guard station buildings and does not mention a lookout tree. The story reports all three accounts.
The Forest Service page says to book through Recreation.gov, but the Recreation.gov listing says the bunkhouse does not offer reservations through Recreation.gov.
The Forest Service page gives both November 14 and November 20 as season end dates, and the story gives both dates.

notes_for_editor: The brief's access 'unknown' is answered only for the rental guard station, not the lookout tree; access.level 'public' refers to booking the cabin. The lookout tree's form and dates conflict across the three history sources and are not reconciled. The Forest Service page itself gives both Nov 14 and Nov 20 as season end dates; the Forest Service and Recreation.gov pages disagree on how to book. Recreation.gov credits the CCC with the 1938 bunkhouse while the Forest Service credits it with 1935 buildings; both are recorded. It is unknown whether the guard station stands on the lookout spot. The firelookout.org index lists a separate 'Summit G.S. Lake' Firefinder entry; it is a different site and was ignored.
